summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with chronic pancreatitis, secondary diabetes due to pancreatic insufficiency, gastroparesis, and bipolar disorder was admitted for worsening right upper quadrant abdominal pain and a syncopal episode. Initial concerns included acute cholecystitis, but a normal HIDA scan ruled this out. The pain was determined to be an acute exacerbation of chronic pancreatitis. During admission, he experienced a hypoglycemic event with blood glucose of 34, manifesting as diaphoresis, tremulousness, and altered responsiveness, which resolved with dextrose. This was attributed to impaired glucagon response from pancreatic insufficiency. A CT neck showed benign bilateral parotid enlargement, likely due to metabolic derangements or recurrent vomiting. His insulin regimen was transitioned to a sliding scale to reduce hypoglycemia risk, and he was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans for diabetes management and surgical evaluation for cholecystectomy.
